name: Plug and jack with common pin number
summary: A plug and jack pair carrying one shared pin number for both halves rather than separate numbers on each half.
description: Some connector symbols carry a single pin number shared by both mating halves, because the pin and socket on a given contact position carry the same number in the connector insert. This keeps schematics uncluttered and matches how most connector manufacturers number inserts.

The common number assumes both halves use matching numbering. Where a harness connector is mated to a board header with different numbering, separate pin numbers are needed. This is a publisher drafting variant, so the underlying connection meaning is the same as an ordinary plug and socket pair.
readingNotes: Confirm both halves use the same pin numbering scheme.
Read the pin number once for both halves.
drawingChecklist: Use common numbering only where the inserts match.
Keep the connector tag on the symbol.
Switch to separate numbers for mismatched pairs.
distinction: The common pin number form carries one number for both halves; the standard pair can carry different numbers per half.
